topStories.headline: Broadway Tunnel Now Operating at Half Capacity as 14-Month Chinatown Construction Push Begins
topStories.dek: A $76 million seismic upgrade to the Chinatown Public Health Center has kicked off a 14-month partial closure of the Broadway Tunnel that will reshape commutes between Russian Hill, North Beach, and Chinatown.
topStories.body:
San Francisco Public Works launched its long-anticipated Broadway Tunnel construction project this week, beginning with a full 24-hour closure on Sunday, August 16, before shifting to a sustained partial closure that transportation officials say will last approximately 14 months. The project is tied to seismic upgrades at the Chinatown Public Health Center at 1490 Mason Street, a building whose structural supports connect directly to the tunnel's eastern entrance.

Starting Monday, August 17, the westbound bore reopened to carry traffic in both directions — one lane each way — while crews work through successive phases. Each bore will be reconfigured in turn over roughly seven months apiece before the project wraps up around October 2027. The SF Chronicle reported that delays are "likely for motorists during peak travel times," and the SFMTA has published a series of regional detour maps for drivers who typically use the tunnel to connect Nob Hill and Russian Hill with the Financial District and downtown.

The Broadway Tunnel construction is one of three simultaneous major projects underway in Chinatown, which together carry a total price tag of $150 million. The other two are the $73 million Portsmouth Square Improvement Project — which already saw the demolition of the 300-foot Kearny Street pedestrian bridge earlier this month — and the renovation of the Chinatown/Him Mark Lai Branch Library. San Francisco Public Works spokesperson Rachel Gordon has described the trio as "one of the city's most significant investments in this historic neighborhood in decades."

For residents of Russian Hill, Nob Hill, and Polk Gulch who regularly use the Broadway Tunnel, the SFMTA recommends alternative routes including northbound Franklin Street to eastbound Bay Street to southbound Columbus Avenue. Muni service on the 8-Bayshore line continues to operate with reroutes in effect. Commuters are urged to check the SFMTA Chinatown Transportation Updates page for the latest detour maps before traveling.

topStories.headline: The Huntington Hotel's Return Puts Two Storied Nob Hill Landmarks Back in Business
topStories.dek: After reopening in March following a six-year closure and a top-to-bottom renovation, the Huntington Hotel has reclaimed its perch atop Nob Hill — just as the InterContinental Mark Hopkins prepares to mark its 100th anniversary in December.
topStories.body:
Nob Hill is experiencing a rare double milestone in 2026: two of its most celebrated hotels are either back or celebrating a centennial. The Huntington Hotel — which shuttered in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic — officially reopened in March after an extensive renovation led by designer Ken Fulk and a new ownership group spearheaded by real estate developer Greg Flynn. Mayor Daniel Lurie attended a ribbon-cutting ceremony and called it "another sign that San Francisco is on the rise."

The renovated Huntington now offers 71 guest rooms and 72 suites, with rooms averaging 581 square feet — well above the industry standard. The iconic Big Four restaurant has returned, celebrating its own 50th anniversary with a revamped menu and a new cocktail salon called Arabella's. The hotel's three-level Nob Hill Spa has also been relaunched as a luxury wellness destination. The Hoodline reported that the hotel "has reclaimed its rightful place in the city's luxury landscape."

Meanwhile, the InterContinental Mark Hopkins is counting down to December 4, 2026, when it will mark its 100th anniversary. As part of the centennial celebration, the legendary Top of the Mark rooftop bar relaunched its famed "100 Martini" passport program on May 25, inviting guests to work through a curated menu of 100 signature cocktails. The 19th-floor lounge, which has commanded panoramic views of San Francisco Bay since 1939, also hosts live entertainment on Saturday evenings.

Together, the two hotels' storylines reflect a broader recovery in Nob Hill's luxury hospitality sector. With the Huntington fully operational and the Mark Hopkins centennial year in full swing, the hilltop neighborhood that was once the domain of Gold Rush railroad barons is again drawing visitors in search of old-world grandeur.

topStories.headline: Chinatown Night Market Named #1 in the Country — Next Edition September 11
topStories.dek: BeChinatown's monthly Grant Avenue street festival, recently voted the nation's top night market for the second consecutive year, continues through October with its next free event on September 11.
topStories.body:
The Chinatown Night Market, a monthly street festival organized by BeChinatown San Francisco and the Civic Joy Fund, has been voted the #1 night market in the country for the second year in a row, according to Funcheap SF. The free event takes over Grant Avenue — from California Street to Pacific Street — on the second Friday of every month from May through October, running 5 to 9 p.m.

With the August 14 installment just passed, the next date is Friday, September 11. The event features five blocks of food stalls, lion dancing, cultural performances, outdoor dining, beer and wine gardens, art, and local merchants. A two-block games and seating area on Waverly Place rounds out the festivities. Organizers say the market draws between 10,000 and 18,000 visitors each month, and features more than 40 local restaurants and merchants, most of them Chinatown-based.

The market is a partnership between the civic nonprofit BeChinatown and the Civic Joy Fund. BeChinatown founder Lily Lo has described the event's purpose as wanting people "to come out to support our small businesses by eating, shopping, and having fun." Beginning in 2025, the market also began showcasing up-and-coming Asian American DJs and performers on a dedicated stage.

The remaining 2026 dates are September 11 and October 9. Admission is free. Grant Avenue is closed to traffic during the event hours.

events.title: RESONANCE: Bill Fontana Sound Installation at Grace Cathedral

events.description: Artist-in-Residence Bill Fontana presents RESONANCE, a sound sculpture created with the cathedral's silent bells and organ pipes. The internationally recognized sound artist has been creating pioneering audio works since the late 1960s.

events.title: Chinatown Night Market
events.description: Free monthly street festival on the second Friday of each month through October, featuring 5 blocks of food stalls, lion dancing, live entertainment, and local merchants. Next date: September 11.

events.title: "Ties vs. High Heels" — Great Star Theater
events.location: Great Star Theater, 636 Jackson St, Chinatown
events.description: A classic Bay Area dark comedy adapted from Silicon Valley playwright Shen Yue's original script, performed at Chinatown's historic nonprofit theater in its 101st year of operation.

events.title: Chinatown Free Sunday Family Block Party w/ Lion Dance
events.description: A free, family-friendly outdoor block party on Grant Avenue featuring a lion dance performance and gifts for attendees, organized by the Chinatown community.

events.title: Chinatown Autumn Moon Festival 2026

events.title: InterContinental Mark Hopkins Centennial Year — Top of the Mark 100 Martini Experience
events.location: Top of the Mark, 999 California St, Nob Hill
events.description: Throughout 2026, the InterContinental Mark Hopkins celebrates its 100th anniversary with curated guest experiences and the revived 100 Martini passport program at the historic 19th-floor rooftop bar. Live entertainment Saturdays (cover fee applies).

moreNews.headline: Portsmouth Square's 'Bridge to Nowhere' Is Gone — Kearny Street Reopened
moreNews.body: The 300-foot concrete-and-steel Kearny Street pedestrian bridge that connected Portsmouth Square to the Hilton Chinatown hotel was demolished in early August, completing a key early phase of the $73 million Portsmouth Square Improvement Project. Nicknamed the "bridge to nowhere" for its underuse, the structure was built in 1971 and was designed by Chinese American architect Chi-Kwan Chen. Its removal adds 20,000 square feet of pedestrian space to the reimagined plaza. SF Public Works says the bridge was taken down in phases, with crews removing it "piece by piece" to ensure safety. Kearny Street between Clay and Washington has since fully reopened to traffic. The Portsmouth Square park itself remains closed through an estimated mid-2028 completion, as the full renovation — which will include a new 8,500-square-foot community clubhouse, a larger playground, and an adult fitness center — continues.

moreNews.headline: Bageletto Opens on Polk Street, Filling Russian Hill's Bagel Gap
moreNews.body: Bageletto, a popular Mission District bagel shop that opened in 2025, has expanded to Russian Hill, taking over a former Peet's Coffee location on Polk Street between Broadway and Vallejo. The SF Standard reported in April 2026 that Bageletto co-founder Kiki Theodorides confirmed the new outpost would open by summer, noting that Russian Hill is a "true bagel desert" despite San Francisco's increasingly competitive bagel scene. Bageletto is known for its house-cured meats, artisan bagel sandwiches, and a larger production facility than its Mission flagship.

moreNews.headline: Chinatown's Three Big Construction Projects: What to Know This Week
moreNews.body: Three simultaneous projects totaling $150 million are reshaping Chinatown's infrastructure. The Portsmouth Square renovation (est. completion mid-2028) has closed the 1.3-acre park for reconstruction including a new community clubhouse, playground, and adult fitness center. The Broadway Tunnel is now in a 14-month partial closure tied to seismic upgrades at the Chinatown Public Health Center at 1490 Mason Street, with one lane in each direction running through a single bore. And the Chinatown/Him Mark Lai Branch Library renovation is also underway. SFMTA has published detailed detour maps at its Chinatown Transportation Updates page. The Muni 8-Bayshore bus continues to operate with reroutes; riders should use Clay and Montgomery as an alternative stop during closures.

restaurants.name: Swan Oyster Depot
restaurants.description: A beloved Polk Gulch institution since 1903, serving fresh oysters, Dungeness crab, clam chowder, and Sicilian sashimi at an 18-stool marble counter — cash-only and no reservations.

restaurants.name: Harris' Restaurant
restaurants.description: An upscale San Francisco steakhouse institution on Van Ness serving USDA prime dry-aged beef, fresh seafood, and classic cocktails in an elegant setting.

restaurants.name: Sorella
restaurants.description: A convivial Italian restaurant at the crest of Polk Street, with a kitchen led by acclaimed chef Suzette Gresham and an inventive cocktail program highlighting Italian spirits.

restaurants.name: Fiorella Polk
restaurants.description: A larger Russian Hill outpost of the beloved Richmond pizzeria, serving airy, light-crusted pies topped with clams, guanciale, and seasonal ingredients alongside a full antipasti menu.

restaurants.name: Mister Jiu's
restaurants.description: A celebrated Michelin-starred Chinatown restaurant by chef Brandon Jew, serving inventive Cantonese cuisine in a beautifully restored 1890s building on Waverly Place.

restaurants.name: China Live
restaurants.type: Chinese culinary marketplace and restaurant complex
restaurants.description: A multi-concept Chinese dining destination on Broadway featuring a main restaurant, Eight Tables fine dining room, Cold Drinks Bar speakeasy, tea lounge, and marketplace.

restaurants.name: R&G Lounge
restaurants.description: A Chinatown institution for over 35 years, serving live Dungeness crab, salt-and-pepper dishes, and classic Hong Kong–style Cantonese seafood in a casual, well-lit dining room.

restaurants.name: Empress by Boon
restaurants.description: An elegant sixth-floor restaurant occupying the historic Empress of China space, offering refined Cantonese cuisine with sweeping skyline views over Grant Avenue.

restaurants.name: Four Kings (四大天王)
restaurants.description: A buzzy modern Cantonese spot from Mister Jiu's alums, serving seven-day dry-aged squab, XO escargot, and beef chow fun to a backdrop of 1990s Canto-Pop.

restaurants.name: Good Mong Kok Bakery
restaurants.description: A beloved takeout-only Chinatown institution famous for its generously stuffed char siu bao, steamed dumplings, and freshly baked pastries at incredibly affordable prices.

restaurants.name: Amélie
restaurants.description: A romantic Polk Street wine bar with a warm, dimly lit atmosphere, a carefully curated natural wine list, and small French-inspired bites popular with locals and expats alike.

restaurants.name: El Lopo
restaurants.description: A fun, convivial Polk Street bar and restaurant with a rotating menu of seasonal cocktails, craft beers, and approachable small plates in a lively neighborhood setting.

restaurants.name: Karam
restaurants.description: A popular Polk Street spot serving traditional Lebanese mezze, grilled meats, and house-baked flatbreads in a warm, neighborhood-friendly setting.

restaurants.name: Dunya Bistro
restaurants.description: An acclaimed Afghan bistro on Polk Street known for its lamb dishes, bolani, and mantu dumplings served in a cozy, warmly decorated dining room.

restaurants.name: Li Po Cocktail Lounge
restaurants.description: A Chinatown landmark since 1937, famous for its potent Chinese mai tais served in paper cups, kitschy red-lantern décor, and cash-only policy.

restaurants.name: Cold Drinks Bar
restaurants.description: A swanky, speakeasy-style Chinatown bar above China Live featuring tuxedoed bartenders, an extensive Scotch menu, and modern Shanghai-meets-old-SF ambiance.

restaurants.name: Goldenette
restaurants.description: A stylish Polk Street restaurant blending Vietnamese and French flavors, praised for creative cocktails and dishes in a beautiful, intimate dining room.

restaurants.name: Bi-Rite Market Polk Street
restaurants.description: A 4,000-square-foot Russian Hill outpost of the beloved SF grocer, stocked with high-quality produce, meats, a sandwich counter, fish and meat cases, and baked goods.

restaurants.name: Bageletto
restaurants.description: The Russian Hill outpost of the popular Mission bakery, serving house-cured meat sandwiches on freshly made bagels from a former Peet's Coffee location on Polk Street.

hotels.name: Fairmont San Francisco
hotels.description: The original Fairmont, perched atop Nob Hill since 1907, offering panoramic bay views, 606 guest rooms and suites, the iconic Tonga Room, Laurel Court afternoon tea, and easy access to all three cable car lines.

hotels.name: InterContinental Mark Hopkins San Francisco
hotels.description: A Nob Hill landmark since 1926, celebrating its centennial year in 2026, with 380 guest rooms, the legendary Top of the Mark 19th-floor cocktail lounge with panoramic city views, and the Nob Hill Club restaurant.

hotels.name: The Huntington Hotel
hotels.description: A storied Nob Hill brick landmark reopened in March 2026 after a six-year closure and complete renovation by designer Ken Fulk, now offering 143 rooms and suites, the revived Big Four restaurant, and the three-level Nob Hill Spa.

hotels.name: Stanford Court San Francisco
hotels.description: A classic Nob Hill hotel occupying the site of Leland Stanford's former mansion, offering contemporary rooms, a restaurant, and a rooftop terrace with city views.

hotels.name: Nob Hill Hotel
hotels.description: Originally established in 1906, this Victorian-style boutique hotel features marble floors, period antiques, evening wine tasting, and an on-site Italian bistro, a short walk from Union Square.

hotels.name: Executive Hotel Vintage Court
hotels.description: A wine-themed boutique hotel on Bush Street near Nob Hill, offering complimentary evening wine receptions, comfortable rooms, and easy access to Union Square and the cable car lines.

hotels.name: Petite Auberge
hotels.description: A charming Nob Hill inn with French provincial décor, gas fireplaces in many rooms, afternoon tea and hors d'oeuvres in the lobby, and a breakfast room downstairs.

hotels.name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
hotels.description: A full-service hotel at the edge of Chinatown and North Beach, formerly connected to Portsmouth Square via the now-demolished Kearny Street pedestrian bridge.

shops.name: Russian Hill Bookstore
shops.description: A Polk Street neighborhood treasure offering a curated selection of used books spanning novels, biographies, cookbooks, children's titles, vintage printings, and greeting cards.

shops.name: The Candy Store
shops.description: A colorful, beloved Polk Street candy boutique stocking an irresistible array of handcrafted chocolates, artisan sweets, and specialty confections in gleaming glass jars.

shops.name: Sui Generis
shops.description: A carefully curated men's and women's designer resale boutique on Polk Street specializing in new, used, and vintage labels sourced from hundreds of different consignors.

shops.name: Stuff (Nob Hill)
shops.type: Vintage furniture and home goods shop
shops.description: A fun, eclectic shop on Pacific Avenue near Polk Street filled with vintage furniture, antiques, decorative objects, and unexpected home goods across a sprawling floor plan.

shops.name: Bi-Rite Market
shops.description: The Russian Hill outpost of San Francisco's beloved specialty grocer, offering premium produce, meats, pantry items, a sandwich counter, fish counter, and baked goods at 2140 Polk Street.

shops.name: Chinatown Kite Shop
shops.description: A longtime Chinatown destination stocking colorful kites, wind socks, silk items, and traditional Chinese toys and souvenirs on Grant Avenue.

shops.name: Ten Ren Tea Company
shops.description: A cornerstone of Chinatown's Grant Avenue, selling dozens of premium loose-leaf teas, tea sets, boba drinks, and accessories from one of the world's most respected tea companies.

shops.name: Far East Flea Market
shops.description: A large and well-stocked Chinatown emporium offering traditional Chinese crafts, silk goods, jade jewelry, Buddha statues, cookware, and an extensive range of decorative items.

shops.name: Ginn Wall Hardware
shops.description: A Chinatown staple hardware store carrying traditional Chinese cookware, clay pots, woks, bamboo steamers, and practical household supplies alongside standard hardware goods.

shops.name: Eastwind Books & Arts
shops.type: Asian American bookstore and cultural arts shop
shops.description: A Chinatown cultural institution carrying Asian American literature, Chinese language books, art prints, and cultural gifts reflecting the history and contemporary life of the community.

artEntertainment.name: Grace Cathedral
artEntertainment.description: An iconic neo-Gothic landmark atop Nob Hill offering self-guided tours, two labyrinths, stunning stained glass, a resident artist program, yoga classes, and regular musical performances.

artEntertainment.name: Great Star Theater
artEntertainment.description: The oldest Chinese American theater in North America, founded in 1924 and revitalized since 2015, presenting Cantonese opera, circus arts, comedy, magic, burlesque, and guzheng concerts in Chinatown.

artEntertainment.name: Chinese Historical Society of America Museum
artEntertainment.description: The oldest and largest Chinese American history museum in the country, housed in architect Julia Morgan's landmark 1932 former Chinatown YWCA building at 965 Clay Street.

artEntertainment.name: Cable Car Museum
artEntertainment.description: A free museum embedded in the working Washington-Mason cable car powerhouse, displaying vintage cars and machinery and offering a look at the live underground cables powering San Francisco's iconic transit system.

artEntertainment.name: Chinese Culture Center of San Francisco
artEntertainment.description: A Chinatown cultural organization promoting Chinese and Chinese American art and culture through rotating gallery exhibitions, public programs, and community events on the third floor of the Hilton San Francisco.

artEntertainment.name: Top of the Mark
artEntertainment.type: Historic rooftop cocktail lounge with live music
artEntertainment.description: The legendary 19th-floor rooftop lounge at the InterContinental Mark Hopkins, offering sweeping 360-degree city views, classic cocktails, and live entertainment on Saturday evenings as part of the hotel's 2026 centennial celebrations.

artEntertainment.name: AURA at Grace Cathedral
artEntertainment.description: An immersive 52-minute sound and light experience that bathes the soaring Gothic interior of Grace Cathedral in music and visual projections, available on select dates.

artEntertainment.name: Tonga Room & Hurricane Bar
artEntertainment.type: Tiki lounge and live music venue
artEntertainment.description: A gloriously kitschy tiki bar at the Fairmont Hotel, featuring a floating stage on an indoor lagoon where a live band plays during simulated tropical rainstorms — a genuine San Francisco original since 1945.

gymsRecreation.name: Nob Hill Yoga
gymsRecreation.description: A plant-filled neighborhood yoga sanctuary in the heart of Nob Hill, offering Power Flow, Yin, and beginner-friendly classes led by experienced instructors in a calming, nature-filled space.

gymsRecreation.name: CorePower Yoga — Nob Hill
gymsRecreation.description: A Nob Hill studio on Van Ness Avenue offering CorePower's signature Hot Yoga, Yoga Sculpt, and Vinyasa Flow classes at the crossroads of Nob Hill, Pacific Heights, and Polk Gulch.

gymsRecreation.name: Crunch Fitness — Polk Street
gymsRecreation.description: A well-equipped Crunch Fitness location at Polk and Union serving Russian Hill and Nob Hill residents with a wide array of cardio and strength equipment, group fitness classes, and personal training.

gymsRecreation.name: Nob Hill Spa (at The Huntington Hotel)
gymsRecreation.type: Luxury hotel spa and wellness center
gymsRecreation.description: Reopened in 2026 as part of the Huntington Hotel restoration, this three-level spa offers massages, facials, body treatments, and a renovated indoor pool in an intimate luxury setting atop Nob Hill.

gymsRecreation.name: Huntington Park
gymsRecreation.description: A gracious, block-long park atop Nob Hill surrounded by Grace Cathedral and the historic hotels, offering shaded benches, a children's play area, and a pleasant place to enjoy sweeping neighborhood views.
gymsRecreation.address: California St & Taylor St, Nob Hill

gymsRecreation.name: Ina Coolbrith Park
gymsRecreation.description: A terraced Russian Hill hilltop park named for California's first poet laureate, offering dramatic stairway gardens, wild plantings, and panoramic views of the bay, Coit Tower, and Alcatraz.
gymsRecreation.address: Vallejo St & Taylor St, Russian Hill

gymsRecreation.name: Macondray Lane
gymsRecreation.type: Historic pedestrian lane and green space
gymsRecreation.description: A charming, leafy pedestrian lane canopied with ferns and flowering trees on Russian Hill — the real-life inspiration for Barbary Lane in Armistead Maupin's "Tales of the City" — perfect for a quiet walk.
gymsRecreation.address: Macondray Ln (Jones to Taylor), Russian Hill

gymsRecreation.name: Portsmouth Square
gymsRecreation.description: Known as "Chinatown's Living Room," this historic 1.3-acre plaza is currently closed through mid-2028 for a $73 million renovation that will add a new community clubhouse, playground, and adult fitness center.

gymsRecreation.name: 24 Hour Fitness — Van Ness
gymsRecreation.description: A full-service 24 Hour Fitness location on Van Ness serving the Nob Hill and Polk Gulch communities with cardio machines, free weights, and group fitness classes around the clock.
